articles.summary: “There’s a group to thank for August’s blockbuster jobs report: women.” That’s how CNBC opened its coverage of the latest employment numbers. The data was clear: Women accounted for 158,000 of the 162,000 jobs added to the American economy in August—or 98 percent of the total. CNBC called it “the latest sign of the growing power of women in the labor market.” You might expect me, a professional matchmaker, to look at those numbers and panic. After all, if women keep advancing economically while men fall behind, who exactly are all these successful women going to marry? I hear some version of this question almost every day. Throughout my 19-years-long career, which has included running a successful matchmaking company , writing several books , and hosting a hit Netflix show , I have set up hundreds of marriages and spoken to thousands of single women. articles.title: Trump pursues last-ditch hunt for voter fraud
articles.author: Brittany Gibson
articles.summary: The Trump administration says Americans should prepare between now and Election Day for a wave of new arrests and prosecutions over alleged non-citizen voter fraud . Why it matters: The Trump administration is deploying hundreds of federal investigators and attorneys to pursue President Trump's long-running fixation — and test a broader Republican claim that tougher enforcement will uncover far more illegal voting. "This initiative is a tier one priority," a Justice Department official told reporters on Tuesday. "It's a top priority for the attorney general and for the White House." The big picture: Across the country, there are now 1,600 open cases of potential voter fraud and 160 people have been arrested, a Homeland Security Investigations official said Tuesday. HSI agents have been requesting and combing through publicly available voter data to find cases of non-citizens registering to vote or voting when they're ineligible. The FBI has been working on these cases too. DOJ has charged 24 immigrants this calendar year following the prioritization, according to agency press releases.
